page.summary: Use position and, if necessary, one health state to interrupt a hook trade or carrying route only when it can avert a hook; leave when the carry or rescue window closes.

verdict.recommendation: Pre-position near a real pathing choke point, verify a teammate can use the delay, and abandon the block if the Killer changes target or route.
verdict.soloQ: Attempt only a clear, immediate save; uncertainty about teammate movement makes extended carry interference especially costly.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call the intended route and blocker before contact so the carried or rescued teammate can convert the delay and others stay on objectives.
verdict.mainWeakness: The Killer can drop the carried Survivor, switch targets or take another hook route while the blocker sacrifices health and objective time.

opening: Identify the actual hook or carry path and whether your body can change the outcome before leaving an objective.

rows.situation: A rescued teammate needs one short opening to leave and you are already positioned to cover that route.
rows.action: Occupy the useful path and take a hit only if it lets the teammate escape the immediate recapture. Peel away once their route is open.
rows.why: Physical presence is the resource; a second down for no route gain loses the trade.

rows.situation: The Killer carries a teammate toward a known hook and your position can force a meaningful detour.
rows.action: Block the relevant path briefly and let the carried teammate exploit the delay; do not chase the Killer across the map for a speculative block.
rows.why: The payoff is prevented hook tempo, not merely contact with the Killer.

rows.situation: The Killer changes hooks, drops the carried Survivor or turns onto you.
rows.action: Leave the failed line, avoid donating a second down and return to the next rescue or objective assignment.
rows.why: The recorded counterplay directly removes the value of overcommitted body presence.

abortWhen: Abort when no reachable route can change the hook or escape result.
Exit after a route change or drop rather than following the Killer indefinitely.

strengths: Good position can exchange one health state for avoided hook tempo.
weaknesses: High positioning and timing cost, especially without communication; the Killer can refuse the expected path.
commonMistakes: Arriving after the carry route is already decided.
Continuing to bodyblock after the Killer drops the Survivor or switches to the blocker.
